name: Jules Wong
life: “I still remember the first rail I fitted to the wall of my own flat.” People around the blocks below Foundry Lofts know Jules by a small Thursday habit. Jules checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I priced the missing rail. My family did the original job and used the cheapest possible ending.
appearance: Jules has a center part and straight chestnut hair, an aquiline nose and a square chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a long navy raincoat. It usually goes with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. When somebody else has the floor, Jules gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in.
personality: Jules is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Jules asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To extend the rail beyond step twenty-eight.
family: Fenn Roche is Jules’s cousin. Jules asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Fenn remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The empty berth*, Fenn says, “I've been selling an imaginary fifth berth in people's daydreams.”
connections: Paula Tan. The building manager has to approve the rail the fitter can actually install.

reactions.response: Jules asks one close relative to check in privately instead of stopping the party for a public inquiry.
